22:- Insulation/pool/spa (batch 3, 17 candidates: 8 insulation, 9 pool/spa). Denver insulation is a crowded, rebate-driven market where nearly every small shop competes on free estimates and Xcel rebate paperwork, creating high inbound quote volume while owners and crews are on ladders or in attics; several reviews literally mention competitors never calling back. Pool/spa is thinner and more fragmented, a mix of franchise systems and true owner-operators, with year-round hot tub culture (weekly water care, Airbnb rentals, winter freeze repairs), so recurring-route operators miss urgent repair calls while driving routes. Both trades lean heavily on phone-first contact pages with few published emails.
32:- Appliance/handyman (batch 3, 21 candidates: 11 appliance, 10 handyman). Appliance repair is urgency-driven: same-day or next-day service, one to three hour arrival windows, phone-first booking; inbound calls arrive hot and a missed ring sends the customer to a competitor. Handyman businesses run on variety: project photos, estimates, and multi-trade job types require qualification and scheduling before dispatch, so their pain is sorting and follow-up rather than pure speed. Both trades are owner-led small teams with little or no office staff; only a handful publish a general email, and owner names are rarely stated, so outreach should lean on personalized angles tied to their posted promises rather than naming decision-makers.
42:- Handyman (Western CO, 4 candidates, 2026-09-09): fall is the busiest booking window: honey-do lists, deck/fence repairs, gutter cleaning, swamp-cooler winterization before the first hard freeze, heat-cable and pipe protection, holiday-guest prep punch lists. Second-home owners in Aspen/Snowmass/Steamboat send photo-based requests from out of town. Core pain: missed calls and slow estimates while the owner is on a ladder, plus estimate follow-up that dies when the day runs long; photo intake and estimate-chasing are the fit. Market is heavy with phone-only operators, directory-only listings, and dead sites; only own sites with a real email or form qualified.
47:- HVAC (Western Colorado, batch 13, 2026-09-09): new segment, 10 verified candidates. Independent, family-run, and employee-owned shops rather than national chains, anchored in Grand Junction, Montrose, Glenwood Springs with spokes into Aspen, Basalt, Durango, Hotchkiss, Cortez. September is the hinge month: furnace tune-ups, install-quote follow-up, first-cold-snap breakdowns, plus ski-town second homes needing reliable service from absentee owners. Nearly every shop runs its own site with a working contact form or published email, so direct outreach is practical. Skip patterns: phone-only own sites, parked/dead/hijacked domains, directory-only listings, and a Wheat Ridge-headquartered branch (Major Heating) deprioritized as not clearly local.
60:- Septic / well / pump (Western Colorado, research batch round 23, 2026-09-11): new segment, 9 qualified. Septic pumping runs on 2 to 5 year recall cycles plus emergency demand; several shops promise free estimates and same-day/emergency service, creating the missed-call pain. 24/7 emergency positioning is everywhere but several shops run office-only hours; after-hours calls are the clearest AI receptionist angle. Durango is a septic hot spot (Durango Septic, Mountain Septic, LePew Four Corners, Alpenglow Gunnison). Well and pump shops (San Juan Pump, Valley Pump) have water-outage urgency: a homeowner with no water calls the next shop if the first rings out. Durango Septic literally brands on answering the phone ("the last thing you want is a voicemail") with a small crew in the field. No scheduling software observed anywhere in the segment; software grades UNKNOWN across the board. Segment is nearly all phone-only (8 of 9); only San Juan Pump (Montrose) has an unblocked contact form, though it is a customer form with no B2B invitation.
72:- Awning / shade / patio covers (Western Colorado, round 55, 2026-09-14): brand-new WCO segment. Specialist pool is genuinely sparse as of September 2026: two deep specialists verified (Canvas Shade in GJ, third-generation since 1949, structured multi-step intake form, owner named on site, the clearest WARM in the pool; Durango Shade Company, Wix site, motorized shade systems by phone), two Montrose-area owner-operators (Alpine Shades, motorized/smart-home products, phone-only; Colorado Awning and Screen, Eclipse retractable specialist, own site failed to render this round), one GJ retractable-awning specialist (Western Slope Shading Solutions, WordPress, no own-site contact found), one Glenwood contractor (Daybreak, aging site, awning is one service line, revamp candidate). Mid-September timing is tail-end for shade sales season (commercial restaurant patio enclosures and residential shade sails sell hardest in spring/early summer); fall angle is commercial patio enclosure and off-season planning. Skip patterns: interior window-treatment showrooms (Ambassador Blind, Shades Done Right, Budget Blinds, Gotcha Covered = franchises), general deck/fence builders, Front Range companies, national manufacturers, directory/lead-broker pages, tent manufacturers.

Pool/spa/hot tub (Western Colorado, research batch round 68, 2026-09-16): 11 qualified, the richest WCO batch in several rounds. 78:- Tree care / arborists (Mesa County corridor re-run, round 100, 2026-09-20): 7 qualified, corridor towns only. Segment heat is high: EAB confirmed on the Western Slope (Carbondale, Sept 2026) is a live market-level demand driver, and the fall pre-winter hazard-tree window is open; September-April is the dormant period for ash pruning/removal per town guidance. Missed-call economics dominate: crews are on ropes or storm work while emergency and tree-health calls land on a single phone line, often outside 7:30-17:00 business hours. ISA certification is the published trust differentiator (GJ and Carbondale government lists). Dead/thin web presence is the norm for independents (one candidate's domain is suspended and for sale while the business still operates). Chain watch: SavATree has absorbed T4, Peak Tree Works, Alpine, and Aspen Tree Service between earlier research and send day; re-verify independence at outreach time, never just at discovery. Email-route yield was 1 of 7 (own-site rule held); the rest are phone-route NEWs or form-only. Note: Highlands Tree Co (Carbondale, HOT, phone-only) is the top phone-route tree candidate; it modernizes its own site (Vercel), so the angle there is intake automation, not revamp.
